title: Cross field via angle-based MI formulation (Campen Ch. 4)
description:
**Depends on PATCH-38.** Stage 1 of the QGP pipeline: produce a smooth 4-RoSy cross field on the input triangulated mesh. Implements Campen 2014 Chapter 4 — the angle-based mixed-integer formulation, NOT the vector-based KCPS form (vector forms restrict valences and admit zero-vector degeneracies).

**Energy (Eq. 4.6):** min Σ_{e_ij ∈ E} ( θ_i − θ_j + κ_ij + m_ij · π/2 )^2
  - θ_i ∈ ℝ per face: tangent angle in local reference frame.
  - κ_ij angular offset aligning frames of face i,j.
  - m_ij ∈ ℤ on a face-cycle basis (one per spanning-tree edge per [BZK09]).
  - Solver: greedy MI of [BZK12] — calls SparseLU + IlpSolver from PATCH-38.

**Outputs:**
- θ per face → 4-RoSy cross field.
- Singularities = vertices where face-cycle holonomy is non-zero. Index_C(s) = K(s)/(2π) ∈ multiples of 1/4. Valence relation: 1 − val(n)/4 = index_C(s).
- Combed field for downstream (single-valued direction with seam + matching).

**Principal-direction alignment (4.2.2):** detect anisotropic regions, hard-fix θ to the principal direction in those triangles. Regions identified per [BZK09].

**Failure modes:**
- Index ≥ 1 from concentrated curvature → split per [BZK09, PZKW11].
- (val-3, val-5, genus-1) edge case → merge per [JT73, MPZ14].

References:
- Algorithm spec: Ixdar/ixdar-tickets/PATCH-37-CAMPEN-SPEC.md (Stage 1 section)
- metriko reference: /tmp/metriko/include/metriko/core/vectorfield/ (~389 LOC C++) — uses KCPS vector form; **deviate from metriko per the thesis**: implement the angle-based [BZK12] MI form.
- Bommes-Zimmer-Kobbelt 2009. Mixed-integer Quadrangulation. SIGGRAPH 2009.
- Bommes-Zimmer-Kobbelt 2012. Practical Mixed-Integer Optimization for Geometry Processing. Curves and Surfaces 2012.
definition-of-done: 1. CrossField class produces θ + singularity list + combed field for any input mesh. 2. Singularities sum to χ(M) (Poincaré-Hopf), validated on torus (sum=0), sphere (sum=2). 3. Smoothness energy below threshold on a flat plane (singularity-free). 4. Skull.obj produces ~50-200 singularities (typical for organic shapes); hand.obj similar. 5. Matches metriko's KCPS output to topological structure (singularity count + indices) on Hand.obj baseline.
testing-plan: 1. Sphere: 8 singularities of index +1/4 (or equivalent valid distribution). 2. Torus: zero net singularity index. 3. Flat plane: zero singularities. 4. Hand.obj: compare singularity count + per-singularity index against metriko's Hand baseline (PATCH-37). Expect topological agreement (counts match), geometric drift OK (positions can vary up to one face).
